sectionsUsed: 8.3 Handling Exceptions: try and except; naming specific exceptions; the else clause runs when the try clause raises no exception
8.4 Raising Exceptions: raise with an exception instance or class
8.7 Defining Clean-up Actions: finally runs whether or not an exception occurred, and an unhandled exception is re-raised after it
ValueError: an argument has the right type but an inappropriate value
TypeError: an operation or function is applied to an object of inappropriate type
Exception: all built-in, non-system-exiting exceptions derive from it; user-defined exceptions should also derive from it
BaseException: KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit derive from BaseException directly
When to use logging: print for ordinary console output of a command-line script; logging for events in a program
Logging levels: DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR, CRITICAL; the default level is WARNING
Advanced logging tutorial: a good convention is logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

What happens if no configuration is provided: the event is output by the handler of last resort, which writes the event description message to sys.stderr (supports the optional anecdote's logger.warning("low stock") output)
Logger.exception(): logs a message with level ERROR and adds exception information; call it only from an exception handler
